title: Oscar and the Monsoon
premise: Dominic Underhill, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Calloway syndicate, is hired by his old rival Maren Voss to guide a convoy across the Kestrel Range before the first snows — a route he swore off after a monsoon flood killed his mentor and half his crew years ago. What begins as a salvage run for a buried weather station's data becomes a reckoning: the records prove the flood was foreseen and suppressed by the same men now financing Dominic's debt. Racing the season's turn, betrayed from within, Dominic must choose between paying what he owes and exposing what was buried, and in the end he delivers the evidence to the flood's survivors rather than to any court, trading his own safety for a justice the law never offered.
about_author: Vesper Montrose is the pen name of a former field researcher who spent six seasons documenting extreme weather in remote mountain corridors before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who trust landscapes more than institutions.

chapters.title: The Debt of Clear Skies
chapters.summary: Dominic Underhill, POV. In a rain-soaked port town, Dominic negotiates yet another extension with Calloway's collectors while his crew patches the convoy trucks. When Maren Voss arrives with a contract for the Kestrel crossing — the route he swore off — pride and desperation war openly. Emotional beat: the humiliation of owing everything to people who smile while they collect.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Maren reveals the job: recover sealed instruments and data cores from Station Nine, drowned in the monsoon flood that killed Dominic's mentor Elias and four crew members. She claims it's salvage; Dominic suspects more. His navigator Priya urges refusal; his mechanic Tomás needs the payout. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing as anger at being bought.

chapters.title: Convoy of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Priya's POV on departure day. The crew — Priya, Tomás, rookie scout Idris, and Maren's quiet fixer Halloran — climbs into the foothills as clouds build over the range. Old markers from the fatal expedition appear where they shouldn't. Emotional beat: the uncanny sense that the mountain has been waiting for them.

chapters.title: Station Nine
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They reach the flooded station and dive the submerged vault; the data cores reveal forecast models proving officials knew the flood was coming weeks early — and suppressed warnings to protect mining interests backed by Calloway money. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of realizing his debt and his dead are entangled.

chapters.title: Halloran's Silence
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Halloran radios ahead, and Idris catches him doing it. The crew realizes someone at Calloway knows what the cores contain. A rockslide — too deliberate — closes the low pass, forcing them onto the high route with the snowline dropping fast. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening into certainty among people who trusted each other.

chapters.title: White Wind
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. An early blizzard traps the convoy on an exposed shelf; Tomás nearly dies repairing an axle in whiteout conditions. Maren finally admits she wasn't hired to salvage — she was hired to make sure nothing came back down the mountain. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against survival, and the strange calm of having nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: The Turn
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Halloran tries to destroy the cores overnight; Idris stops him, and in the struggle Halloran falls into a crevasse. Dominic saves the data but loses the radio. With Calloway's second team ascending behind them, the crew splits the load and pushes for the high col. Emotional beat: the moment retreat becomes impossible and purpose hardens.

chapters.title: Elias's Route
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, the only chapter inside her head. Following a shortcut Elias once mapped, Maren confesses her own role in burying the forecasts years ago — she signed the suppression order to save her company, and this crossing is her penance. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken aloud, and refused absolution.

chapters.title: The Col Before Snowfall
chapters.summary: Climax. Dominic's POV. Calloway's team corners them at the col; a standoff in the storm ends when Priya triggers a controlled avalanche that buries the pursuers' vehicles without killing the men. The crew crosses as the passes close behind them forever. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into precision — justice delivered by the landscape itself.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Resolution. Priya's POV. Downvalley, Dominic gives the cores not to lawyers or press but to the flood survivors' assembly in the river towns, letting them decide how to use the truth. He walks away still owing Calloway, but no longer owned. Emotional beat: quiet, costly peace — memory honored, justice placed in the hands it always belonged to.
